reranked_evidence.title: consistency - Which way locks? / Which way is locked? - User Experience Stack Exchange
reranked_evidence.snippet: * The keyhole on the other side of a door lock. I've seen doorknobs have all sorts of configurations of this, so it never feels natural to lock or unlock someone else's door. The best thing for UX would be to have it be consistent across all locks. What I *really* want is to not feel like an idiot when I unlock a door and *try* to open it, only to realize I just locked it. * Well, there is no de facto rule - it could go either way, but I'll assume "the most usable direction." :) Though, now that I think about it I'm trying to visualize a lock mechanism that would work in correctly going the "wrong" way (short answer: clockwise = lock, counterclockwise = unlock). The first point to make is that there is no standard in the way which locks turn in order to lock or unlock. When it is in a horizontal position, the door is locked.
